chunks: By this chain of narration, from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab, from Uthman b. Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).

He said: Whoever swears by Allah must be truthful, and whoever is not truthful will have nothing with Allah. Whoever has someone swear to him by Allah must be pleased, and whoever is not pleased will have nothing with Allah.

key_terms.فليس من الله في شئ: will have nothing with Allah — an expression meaning complete loss of divine connection

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about swearing by Allah and being truthful?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq teaches that oaths by Allah carry a dual obligation: the one swearing must be truthful, and the one receiving the oath must accept it. Failure in either case severs one's connection with Allah, emphasizing both the sanctity of oaths and the duty of trust between believers.

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab from `Uthman b. `Isa from Abi Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as).

He said: Whoever swears by Allah must be truthful, and whoever is not truthful will have nothing with Allah. Whoever has someone swear by Allah must be pleased [with the outcome], and whoever is not pleased will have nothing with Allah.
